tldr: WILBUR is a web agent that uses adaptive in-context learning with a trained demonstration ranking model, instruction synthesis from positive and negative examples, and an intelligent backtracking mechanism to improve task success rates on real websites.
contributions: First web agent to recover from delayed mistakes via graph exploration-based backtracking to previous navigational states
Demonstration ranking model that re-ranks action demonstrations using embeddings of observations, plans, and actions to predict success likelihood
Synthesis of both positive and negative demonstrations into succinct instructions to maximize context window utility
First application of an LLM-based autocurriculum with automatic scoring to generate training data without human annotation for web agents
State-of-the-art text-only result of 53% on WebVoyager, beating prior text-only approaches by 8%
methods: WILBUR operates as a browser-based agent using a domain-specific language for web actions. At each step, it retrieves goal-conditioned and website-conditioned demonstrations (both successful and unsuccessful) from a knowledge bank using cosine similarity, then re-ranks action demonstrations with a trained MLP ranking model that combines observation, plan, and action embeddings to predict execution success. A synthesizer LLM distills demonstrations into concise instructions. An actor LLM predicts the next action, an executor runs it via a browser interpreter, and a reflection module assesses whether the action contributed progress, triggering backtracking to the most recent URL-based state if needed. An autocurriculum generates goals conditioned on website DOMs, runs the agent, and uses an LLM self-evaluator to score trajectories, training the ranking model on binary cross-entropy loss.
results: WILBUR achieves 53% on the WebVoyager benchmark (643 goals across 15 real websites), which is a new text-only state-of-the-art, surpassing the previous best by 8%. Performance gains vary by website, reaching up to 36% on certain sites. It performs within 5% of a strong multi-modal model despite using only textual inputs. Backtracking and loop detection improves performance by 6% over a baseline with retrying but no backtracking. Adaptive in-context learning and autocurriculum contribute an additional 12% improvement. The zero-shot baseline is outperformed by 18% overall.
limitations: Only receives textual inputs (DOM text) and does not use screenshots, yet still reaches within 5% of a multi-modal model
Not all state changes can be reverted during backtracking because the backend is real rather than simulated; only states corresponding to navigation events (URL changes) can be returned to
Substantial number of failures are attributed to engineering challenges of operating the web rather than reasoning limitations
Context window limits the number of demonstrations that can be included
